title: Setup wizard command and its copy are duplicated across README, docs and UI; change them together
answers: where is the mlflow setup wizard command defined
I changed the README setup command, what else must change
why is README_SKINNY.md out of date
en.json message IDs changed after editing agent card copy
body:
- The wizard command `curl -LsSf https://mlflow.org/wizard/setup.sh | sh` and its companion copy appear in README.md, libs/skinny/README_SKINNY.md, the tracing quickstart and regression-testing MDX pages, and the agent action card.
- AGENT_SETUP_COMMAND in AgentActionCard.tsx holds the UI command string; the card's tab label and description are FormattedMessage strings.
- libs/skinny/README_SKINNY.md is a generated copy of the top-level README. Edit README.md and regenerate the skinny README rather than hand-editing it.
- Each changed defaultMessage or description in AgentActionCard.tsx changes its hashed ID in mlflow/server/js/src/lang/default/en.json. Regenerate en.json; the old IDs are removed and new ones added.
- Each surface words its companion copy separately, so keep the claims consistent across them rather than expecting identical text.
applies: Any change to the setup command, its companion copy, or the agent action card strings in the OSS onboarding surfaces.
says: The setup command on the onboarding card does not match the documentation website.
Update the terminal setup snippet across the onboarding screen and the quickstart guide.
The agent action card in the web interface shows outdated setup instructions.
Change the setup wizard command everywhere across the application interface and documentation.
Onboarding card description text is missing updated copy after modifying the setup instructions.

AGENT_SETUP_COMMAND in AgentActionCard.tsx stores the UI command string, while tab labels and descriptions are FormattedMessage strings whose hashed IDs require regenerating mlflow/server/js/src/lang/default/en.json. libs/skinny/README_SKINNY.md is generated from README.md and must be regenerated rather than hand-edited.
